analysis: In the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), prostacyclin analogues are used to mimic the effects of prostacyclin, a natural vasodilator. Iloprost, Treprostinil, and Epoprostenol are all known prostacyclin analogues. Riociguat, however, is not a prostacyclin analogue; it is a soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator. This class of drug works by a different mechanism, enhancing the nitric oxide pathway to cause vasodilation and reduce pulmonary blood pressure. The enhanced information aligns with standard medical knowledge, confirming that Riociguat is the drug among the options that is not a prostacyclin analogue.
